params.body:
## Why

Two things Shane saw on the damage tab of the vehicle sheet on staging after #267: a location that
carries damage was not marked on the car diagram, and a form from another screen (Naam, Straat,
**Nr.**, **Postcode**) sat on top of the damage card.

## Cause of each

**1. The mark hung on a page wrapper, not on the damage tab.** #267 dropped `btn btn-circle-lg
btn-circle` from the diagram buttons, so the only thing that still says "this location has damage" is
`.ui-edit .car_explosion_button.btn-warning` in `refresh.css`. `.ui-edit` is a page wrapper, not part
of the partial: it lives on `ownstock/create.blade.php`, `ownstock/edit.blade.php` and
`ownstock/vehicle_form_preview.blade.php`. Rendering both paths shows the markup and the wrapper are
correct today (`btn-warning` on button 15 in both, `.ui-edit` an ancestor in both, amber in the
browser), so the mark is not lost on main — but it is one include away from being lost silently, and
a state you have to see may not depend on an ancestor the partial does not bring along.

**2. The sheet's dialogs stay open across a step change.** `#locationModal`, `#createCarVweModal`,
`#relationModal` and `#editImageModal` are rendered next to the Livewire component, not inside it. Open
"nieuwe locatie" on the Algemeen step, then go to Schade: Livewire re-renders the fields *behind* the
dialog and nobody closes it, so the location form keeps floating over the damage tab with its backdrop
dimming the card underneath. Reproduced in a browser on `origin/main` (see the before shot: Nr. 35,
Postcode 9991 over the damage diagram). There is no `<table>` anywhere on the vehicle sheet and
"Postcode" appears exactly once in the rendered page, in this dialog, so this is the only place that
markup can come from.

A second, quieter version of the same kind of leak: `damage`, `photos` and `options` were the only
`.tab-pane` siblings without a `wire:key`, while their keyed siblings appear and disappear per step.
An ignored island the morph pairs with another pane keeps that other pane's DOM — foreign markup in
the damage tab without a line of blade being wrong.

## What

- `refresh.css`: the diagram rules (`car_explosion_button`, its `btn-warning` and `btn-info` states,
  `car_explosion`, `#button_18`, `car_explosion_image`) hang on `.ui-damage-layout`, the container the
  damage partial renders itself, instead of on `.ui-edit`. Every other `.ui-edit`-scoped rule is
  untouched (there are ~320 of them, from `.ui-edit .card` to the wizard steps; dropping the scope
  wholesale would restyle every screen that uses those classes). It cannot leak: `.ui-damage-layout`
  exists only in `ownstock/_tabs/damage.blade.php`, and the other damage screens (stocklist, website,
  offertes) still carry the old `.btn btn-warning btn-circle` markup under `.car_explosion_stocklist`.
  The three runtime states `vehicle.js` swaps (`btn-secondary` / `btn-warning` / `btn-info`) keep
  their look: neutral, has damage, currently open.
- `livewire/vehicle-form.blade.php`: a step change closes the dialogs the sheet itself opened
  (`sluitFicheModals()` in `ga()`, the one funnel every step change goes through). Which dialogs are
  ours is a question to the DOM, not a list to maintain: everything open in the sheet's page section
  closes, the layout's own dialogs (the terms a user has to accept, appended to the body) are left
  alone.
- `livewire/vehicle-form.blade.php`: `wire:key="pane-damage|pane-photos|pane-options"` on the three
  island panes, so no pane can ever be paired with another pane's DOM.
- `tests/Feature/DamageTabTest.php`: six tests. A location with a note renders `btn-warning` and the
  other locations do not, in both the Livewire sheet and the classic edit page; the rule that paints it
  is scoped on the damage container and no longer on `.ui-edit`; the rendered damage island holds no
  table, table header or location-form field from another screen; every step change closes the sheet's
  dialogs; every island pane carries its own key.

Names, ids, `wire:` and `onclick` handlers are untouched, and "changes to damage are saved
immediately" still runs over the same `addDamage` round trip.

## Screenshots

Damage tab at 1280 and 390, before and after, same vehicle with one damage on location 15:
`damage2-before-1280.png`, `damage2-after-1280.png`, `damage2-before-390.png`, `damage2-after-390.png`.
Before: the Nieuwe-locatie form (Nr. 35, Postcode 9991) over the damage tab. After: the damage tab,
location 15 amber, the card with its own note and its own two buttons.

## Checked

- `php artisan view:cache` (415 templates) plus `php -l` on every compiled view: no failures.
- `npm run build` (Vite + purged theme CSS); `public/build` stays untracked.
- `php artisan test --filter='SmokeTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest|UiApiUsageTest|ClassReferencesResolveTest|VehicleForm|Vehicle|Damage'`
  against a MySQL loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations:
  16 passed, 0 failed.
- The new tests bite: on `origin/main` three of the six fail (the CSS scope, the dialog close, the
  island keys); the two markup tests pass there, which is right — the markup was never wrong.
- Reproduced and verified in a real browser (Livewire sheet, logged in): open the location dialog on
  Algemeen, switch to Schade. Before: the dialog is still `display: block` over the damage tab. After:
  it is closed, the terms dialog outside the sheet is untouched, location 15 is still amber and the
  card still reads "15. Links voorwiel / Test".
params.title: Damage tab: highlight back, and no stray table in the card
